## HOME-B1 — missing descendant under an existing aliased home escapes distinctness

validate_distinct_homes checks lexical starts_with, then compares actual paths only if **both full home paths canonicalize**. With Account directory already present and proposed Key path `ACCOUNT/new-key`, the case-aliased parent is the same actual Account directory, but new-key is absent. Whole-key canonicalization fails and actual comparison is skipped. Thus the known ancestor overlap is accepted before setup. A future after-setup Root check does not establish the required constructor/before-setup predicate or prevent this proposed location being prepared inside another home.

Exact actual Rust control: account exists/prepared; new-key leaf absent; std::fs::metadata of its ACCOUNT parent has equal device/inode to account; Rust canonical parent equals account. validate_distinct_account_homes returns **Ok(())**, while required refusal assertion fails. Genuine unrelated missing sibling returns Ok and passes. This is a current ordinary non-racing filesystem source fact, not hostile future replacement.

Required repair: compare existing actual ancestry/prospective missing suffixes so a known aliased ancestor cannot masquerade as an unrelated home. Preserve missing genuinely separate sibling readiness, whole-set Account/Key/Probe checks, explicit native paths and no registry/default layout. Do not solve via lowercasing strings or rejecting all missing paths. Root rechecks at actual binding/use remain required, and no adversarial atomicity claim is added.

## HOME-B2 — resource self-target via aliased existing parent escapes constructor

OwnedHomePlan::new rejects shared source paths only by lexical starts_with(home_path). For receiving directory already present and explicit config target `RECEIVING/config.toml`, the parent canonicalizes to that very receiving directory while leaf is absent. Case-preserved supplied bytes do not lexically start with receiving. Constructor accepts this own-home resource source despite its stated no-self-source invariant. It can consequently allow creation of a self-referential/broken link rather than rejecting the invalid source plan before setup; ordinary missing targets outside the home must remain supported.

Exact actual Rust control verifies missing config leaf and canonical parent==receiving home; **constructor accepted=true**. No prepare/write was performed for this bad resource plan. Required repair: enforce actual/prospective receiving containment for explicitly supplied target paths, including aliased existing parent with missing leaf; retain lossless native source, user-resource symlinks outside the receiver, visible genuine missing state and create-only behavior. This is not a new permission/gate or native target-proof criterion.
